artworks.what_we_see: This painting shows an elderly man dressed in a blue and red marching band uniform, playing a golden trumpet. He wears a matching cap that is topped with a soft, feathery red decoration. His face shows deep wrinkles, and his eyes are focused as he blows into the instrument. The background shows a warm, glowing sunset with a curtain and a small table holding a few objects. The painting is done in a realistic style, with careful attention to the textures of the skin, uniform, and instrument.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artist used warm colors like orange and yellow throughout the background, which contrasts with the cooler blue tones of the uniform. This contrast makes the man and his uniform stand out clearly against the glowing sunset. Fine details in the face, hands, and instrument show a high level of skill in realistic painting. The soft, feathery decoration on his cap adds a small but noticeable detail to his uniform. The warm lighting throughout the artwork creates a nostalgic and intimate atmosphere.
artworks.our_interpretation: This painting captures a sense of dedication and passion for music, shown through the man’s expression while playing. The wrinkles on his face suggest years of experience, possibly hinting a lifetime of performing or practicing his craft. The formal uniform, complete with its decorated cap may represent tradition, discipline, and pride in his role as a musician. The warm, glowing background adds a feeling of nostalgia, as if recalling a memory from the past. Overall, the painting reflects the quiet dignity and joy found in dedicating one’s life to music.
artworks.our_judgement: This painting is successful in portraying both the realistic detail and emotional depth of its subject. The lifelike look in the man’s face, uniform, and instrument makes the piece feel personal or relatable to the viewers. The warm color palette effectively creates a nostalgic and inviting mood that complements the subject. The composition keeps the focus clearly on the musician without unnecessary distractions in the background. All in all, this artwork effectively honors the dedication and artistry of everyday musicians.

artworks.what_we_see: The sculpture is composed of small wooden houses stacked together that are sticking out in different angles. The individual houses vary in colors such as teal, orange, yellow, pink, blue, mint green, purple, brown, gray and white while the roof of each home is painted in neutral colors such as black, brown and beige. The whole structure rests on thin metal rod supports mounted to a wooden rectangular base, which bears an engraved/carved signature.
artworks.personal_analysis: The sculpture is made from the repetition of a single form, a small rectangular house module varied in size, roofline and tilt. The differences within similar subjects create rhythm while preventing monotony. Color helps activate that rhythm. The artist distributes bright contrasting hues like teal, magenta, orange, yellow and mint across the individual houses, which guides the eye and creates a sense of movement throughout the piece. The sculpture is balanced in a way that feels unstable. The large grouping of houses extends outward from a narrow central column and is supported only by thin metal rods rather than a solid base. This contrast between the heavy appearance of the wooden forms and the thinness of the supports beneath them makes the whole structure feel delicate and as if it could fall. There is no single focal point, so the arrangement emphasizes density and accumulation.
artworks.our_interpretation: The sculpture evokes the feeling of a densely packed neighbourhood, a community that was not created with a plan but rather built over time and on a whim, which is why the houses are scattered on the hillside. The whole sculpture being held by thin rods instead of a solid base suggests the fragility and instability of the community, hinting at the vulnerability of its situation. It feels like a nod to the neighbourhoods in the Philippines, how some communities often found themselves jammed together in an attempt to make do with what they have, even if it means enduring cramped conditions just to have a place to stay. As Filipinos are commonly described to be resilient, this artwork becomes an extension of the struggles such communities face in their day-to-day life. The fragile base shows how uncertain life can be in these communities, while the bright colors and lively arrangement show their energy and togetherness.
artworks.our_judgement: The sculpture was able to invoke the feeling of familiarity from the get go.Its composition is strikingly similar to neighbourhoods found in rural cities, transforming a common sight into a visually thoughtful form that pushes the audience to reflect on the social reality it implies. The tightly packed houses feel almost suffocating, yet the vibrant colors suggest otherwise. It used the right palette to highlight the contrast between harsh reality and community resilience. It takes a lot of creativity and skill to make a piece look intentionally unbalanced, and the thin metal rods show the technical ability needed to balance it on an unstable pole. It is impactful because it shifts the focus from hardship to the adaptability and resourcefulness of informal communities.

artworks.artwork_title: Can I Take Your Order Please?
artworks.what_we_see: The painting features a portrait of a humanoid figure. Its head is shaped like a cassette tape with a yellow and red casing labeled “TDK” and “C90” along the bottom front of the casing. The cassette has two large cartoon eyes, and its glasses are made from teal magnetic tape film spilling out from inside the cassette. On top of the cassette rests a small burger topped with a tiny red cap. The figure's body appears to be a connected segmented tube, with red strands of magnetic tape spilling out and looping down toward the shoulders. The figure wears a red and gray collared work shirt/jacket with a small red-and-yellow striped shoulder patch and a tiny embroidered logo of a mascot on the chest. The background is a simple landscape: blue sky with two clouds, distant purple hills, a yellow/green striped field, and two small dark trees.
artworks.personal_analysis: The painting is defined by contrasting lines. Harsh geometric lines form the cassette's rectangular shape and internal divisions, while soft organic strokes define the rest of the figure, such as the spilling magnetic tape and the folds of the shirt. This contrast carries over into shape. The head is composed of geometric forms like the rectangular cassette and circular eyes and glasses, while the body is rendered with softer organic forms that highlight the duality between mechanical and human. The artist also uses warm cool color contrast, where the warm orange red shirt and tan bun stand out against the cool blue sky and teal glasses, which separates the figure from the background. Texture varies from the smooth glossy surface of the cassette to the woven fabric of the shirt and the soft matte bun. The centered and symmetrical composition creates a stable portrait-like presence despite its surreal subject, with emphasis placed on the cartoonish eyes as the only lifelike feature. Finally, the flat minimal background provides negative space that isolates the figure and allows it to dominate the frame.
artworks.our_interpretation: The painting can be read as a surrealist image of a fast food worker. From the Yum burger that is placed on top of its head to the recognizable Jollibee uniform and logo, the figure is supposed to be an embodiment of an employee in the fast food industry. By turning the head into a cassette tape, it raises different interpretations that bear the same essence. It goes to show how workers in the customer service industry are often seen as replaceable, as every day they repeat the same routine, say the same things to please the masses. In this artwork however, the cassette tape has its magnetic tape spilling out, suggesting exhaustion and burnout. While the bright colors and cartoonish eyes give it a playful look at first, underneath it expresses tiredness and the loss of individuality that comes with repetitive service work.
artworks.our_judgement: The artwork was able to successfully express the social message it was trying to convey by simply making the right choice in choosing what object to use in delivering the metaphor. The usage of the cassette tape as a narrative device was smart and original as it is usually an object that is used to record and playback audio. While being an unusual comparison, putting the two together undoubtedly showcases the similarities. What makes this effective is the playful style that was chosen in creating the artwork. At first glance, it pulls the viewer in with its bright colors and, yet the small details unveil the truth piece by piece.

artworks.location: Parokya ni Santa Rosa de Lima (Santa Rosa, Laguna)
artworks.what_we_see: Painted panels on the church’s curved ceiling. Each one shows an apostle’s face with written names above it(San Judas Tadeo, San Mateo and San Simon), framed in gold arches. Painted in realistic form.
artworks.personal_analysis: The colors are simple browns and golds, matching the wood carvings around them. The panels are in the same shape. The apostles are not drawn in a fancy or detailed way, they’re plain and labeled.
artworks.our_interpretation: This is an old-school teaching tool for people who go to the churches to recognise and know the apostles, by using arts and displaying them in every church. San Judas Tadeo is known as the patron saint of the desperate. San Mateo symbolizes transformation and forgiveness, he was a tax collector before becoming a disciple. And San Simon is linked with dedication to his faith. With these three all together, It gives people a quiet reassurance that transformation, dedication, and faith are all watching over the people.
artworks.our_judgement: This kind of art makes the church more sacred and to quietly teach. The fade and cracks in the ceiling and painting, can show how old the church is and the painting. Displaying the painting to the ceiling makes it more eye-catching, instead of putting it on the walls, putting it in the ceiling makes it more reasonable because people look up when they pray so once they pray one of the first things they will see are the paintings.

artworks.what_we_see: The artwork shows a traditional dapilan, a machine used by sugarcane farmers to extract juice from sugarcane. It has large wooden parts placed on top of a thick wooden base. The object has a simple and rough appearance, with visible marks and details on the wood. It is displayed together with other traditional objects in the area.
artworks.personal_analysis: This is mainly made of wood and has a simple but strong structure. It uses two wooden cylinders that squeeze the sugarcane to extract its juice. The machine can be powered by a carabao or cow that moves around it in a circular motion. Although there are other dapilan with different designs, they serve the same purpose of extracting sugarcane juice. Its design shows how traditional tools were made to be useful while using materials that were available to the people.
artworks.our_interpretation: The dapilan shows how people in the past used simple tools to help them in their work. It shows the hard work and skills of sugarcane farmers, especially in processing the sugarcane. Since it is also part of the culture of Ilocano farmers, It became more than just a machine they used for work. It also became part of their way of life and identity.
artworks.our_judgement: The dapilan shows a good example of simple design that can have an important purpose for many. With is wooden structure and traditional way of working, it shows the creativity and skills of the people before. It also shows how people used the materials they had to create something useful for their work. Compared to what we have today, I believe the dapilan can be a bridge between the old way of working and the technology we have now, showing how simple tools before became more advanced and easier to use today.

artworks.what_we_see: The artwork shows a bright day in a rice field, where several women are working together to harvest palay. They are wearing colorful clothes and hats while working in the field. The rice field covers most of the foreground, while a small nipa hut, trees, and mountains can be seen in the background. The painting also has a bright sky and uses different colors, such as green, yellow, orange, blue, and pink. The women are shown doing their work and helping one another during the harvest.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artwork is made using oil paint on canvas. The artist uses bright and vibrant colors, especially green, yellow, blue, orange, and pink, which make the painting look lively and cheerful. The artist also uses different shapes and textures to create the rice fields, trees, and other elements in the surroundings.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork expresses the importance of our farmers, especially the women who work in the fields. Since the Philippines has many agricultural lands and rice is one of the main foods of Filipinos, the painting reminds us of the people behind the food that we eat every day. The women working together also represent the Filipino spirit of bayanihan, showing how people can help one another in doing difficult work.
artworks.our_judgement: The painting leaves a positive and meaningful message about farming and Filipino culture. The bright colors and unique style make the painting lively and interesting, while the women working together clearly show the importance of cooperation and bayanihan. I also think the artwork is effective because it makes the viewers appreciate the hard work of farmers and the people who grow and harvest the food that we eat.

artworks.location: Santa Rosa de Lima Parish Church (Santa Rosa, Laguna)
artworks.what_we_see: This sculpture shows the Virgin Mary holding the lifeless body of her son, Jesus Christ across her lap. Mary is dressed in a white gown with a black veil and crown, while her face shows tears streaming down her cheeks. Jesus is shown with long dark hair and a beard with his eyes closed, and visible wounds with blood on his chest, knees, and feet. He wears a thin white cloth wrapped around his waist, while the rest of his body remains bare. His arms hang loosely, with one resting across Mary’s lap and the other lying to the side as Mary looks downward at him with one arm gently supporting his body.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artist arranges Mary in an upright position while Jesus’ body lies across her, creating a strong contrast in direction that draws attention to his lifeless form. The pale, smooth skin of both figures is emphasized through realistic details, especially in the wounds and blood in Jesus’ body that stand out against his skin. Mary’s white gown contrasts with her black veil, adding to the visual balance of light and dark within the artwork. The way Jesus’ arms lie open, resting away from his body, emphasizes the weight and lifelessness of his form, reinforcing the emotional heaviness of the sculpture. The two figures create a composition that draws the viewer’s eyes from Jesus’ lifeless body to Mary’s crying face, guiding their attention through the entire scene.
artworks.our_interpretation: This sculpture conveys deep sorrow and grief centered on Mary’s mourning over the death of her son. Mary’s tearful expression and gentle hold on Jesus’s body suggest both her sadness and her tenderness as a mother. The visible wounds on Jesus’ body serve as a reminder of his suffering and sacrifice, adding to the emotional impact of the scene. The way his arms lie open and lifeless may symbolize the full surrender of his life and the depth of his sacrifices. The close arrangement of the two figures invites viewers to reflect on themes of loss, sacrifice, and unconditional love.
artworks.our_judgement: This artwork is successful in portraying a deeply emotional and solemn scene. The realistic detail in both figures, from Mary’s tearful face to Jesus’ wounded body makes the piece feel lifelike. The way Jesus’ arms are positioned, lying open and lifeless effectively conveys the full weight of his sacrifice. The close arrangement of the two figures keeps the focus on their emotional connection, strengthening the message of the artwork. Overall, the sculpture clearly communicates its intended message of sorrow, sacrifice, and faith.

artworks.location: Museo de Santa Rosa (Santa Rosa, Laguna)
artworks.written_by: Francisco, Athaliah L. & Mendoza, Juliana Paula B.
artworks.what_we_see: The object is a vintage manual mechanical typewriter resting on top of a wooden desk. It features a tiered QWERTY keyboard just like in today's keyboard but with circular, white-lettered black keys housed inside an angled metal chassis. At the upper section of the machine, an open mechanism reveals the typebars and ribbon spools, followed by a long horizontal rubber platen roller and carriage assembly. Accompanied by an informational museum card placed behind it, the metal body shows significant signs of age, including peeling paint, scratches, and dust.
artworks.personal_analysis: The rust, worn keys, and yellowed nameplate attest to decades of use, turning a common office tool into a relic of local government history. Its value is purely material and evidentiary. The fades of other letters also shows how it is important and well used by Romea Moran.
artworks.our_interpretation: Romeo Moran's decades of municipal record-keeping and the typewriters' placement in a heritage display demonstrate the community's appreciation for maintaining an administrative history. Keeping it intact on how it looks like before, without enhancing anything shows how they want to preserve how it looks when it has been left.
artworks.our_judgement: In my judgment, this artwork is successful because of how it connects us to the past and evokes nostalgia in an era of rapid technological advancement. In an ever-changing world where older tools are quickly phased out in favor of newer innovations, displaying this object provides a meaningful opportunity to understand early trades, remember how past generations lived and worked, and reflect on the evolution of society. Beyond its historical significance, the piece succeeds as an example of applied art due to its exceptional mechanical durability and practical design.

artworks.location: Museo de Santa Rosa (Santa Rosa, Laguna)
artworks.what_we_see: The artwork shows two Filipino women wearing traje de mestiza, which is an elegant version of the baro’t saya. One woman is sitting in front while the other one is behind her. They are wearing traditional dresses with detailed designs and shawls over their shoulders. They also have their hair neatly styled and are wearing accessories. The artwork is in black and white and has a simple background, making the two women and their clothes easy to notice.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artwork appears to be a detailed black-and-white drawing or illustration. The artist uses lines and shading to show the details of the women's faces, hair, and traditional clothes. The different shades of gray also help give the figures depth and make them stand out from the background. I also noticed the detailed patterns on their clothes, which show the traditional fashion during the Spanish period.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork seems to showcase the clothing worn during the Spanish colonial era in the Philippines. It shows the mix of Filipino and Spanish cultures and how people expressed their identity through their traditional clothing. The artwork also shows how proud the Filipinas were of their culture and uniqueness, which allows people today to appreciate and remember their heritage.
artworks.our_judgement: The artwork clearly shows what the subjects are trying to express. In my view, there is a specific emotion we feel when we look at these illustrations as the new generation, seeing Filipinas wearing their traditional clothing. It makes us appreciate their culture and uniqueness, while they continue to be remembered in the present.

artworks.what_we_see: The artwork is a horizontal, framed wood inlay that shows the cityscape of Paris. It is framed by natural wood and has the Arc de Triomphe in the lower left foreground and the iconic Eiffel Tower in the middle. These landmarks are surrounded by geometric multi-story buildings and houses with pointed roofs and small square windows. The composition utilizes various cuts of wood displaying alternating shades of tan, beige, brown,and dark colored woods. The ground shows swirling patterns while the sky area is composed of lighter, horizontal wood tones.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artist uses a similar or close color scheme, grain patterns, and tactile textures of different wood species rather than paint to build form and values.Instead of painting, the artist creates form and values using a similar or close color scheme, grain patterns, and tactile textures of various wood species. While the depth is created by using proportion and scale, the Arc de Triomphe is made larger and placed in the foreground, directing the viewer's gaze diagonally toward the smaller, centrally located Eiffel Tower in the distance.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork expresses a sense of warmth and a nostalgic view of Paris and urban life. By using organic timber and an earthy color scheme, the piece softens the rigid stone and steel typically associated with the city. Through the natural grain and fluid contours of the wood, the composition transforms cold, modern urban spaces into an inviting and timeless charm.
artworks.our_judgement: The use of wood intarsia is remarkably successful because of the high level of craftsmanship required for this kind of artwork. With the artist's expertise, natural wood grains are skillfully selected and aligned to mimic details such as the sky, perspective lines, and building shadows while maintaining structural clarity. This approach effectively combines traditional woodworking techniques with creative architectural abstraction, producing a piece that is visually engaging, tactile, and aesthetically balanced.

artworks.artwork_title: Parokya ni Santa Rosa de Lima / Santa Rosa de Lima Parish Church
artworks.location: Santa Rosa De Lima Parish Church (Santa Rosa, Laguna)
artworks.what_we_see: The photo captures the Santa Rosa de Lima Parish Church at night, where the church is highlighted by warm architectural illumination coming from the lights. The left picture features the side of the church wherein a detached stone bell tower or belfry can be seen and fronted by perimeter fencing and religious statues. The right picture captures the multi-tiered facade of the church, characterized by symmetrical pilasters, arched openings, and topped by the illuminated cross. While people and streetlamps occupy the paved courtyard in front of the church.
artworks.personal_analysis: The architecture demonstrates symmetry and balance through repetitive vertical pilasters and horizontal cornices that counterbalance the heavy stone facade. Constructed from adobe blocks, bricks, and mortar, the thick masonry base creates a rugged, tactile texture characteristic of the Neoclassical-Baroque tradition. Dominated by neutral stone grays and warm undertones, the structure achieves a sense of unity and harmony. At night, warm artificial lighting highlights the rich texture of the stone walls while establishing the glowing rooftop cross as the primary focal point.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork expresses enduring faith, sanctuary, and community identity. With the artwork captured at night, the fortress-like architecture evokes a feeling of safety and permanence built to withstand natural calamities across centuries. The church's warm and radiant lights act as a beacon of hope, guidance, and comfort amidst the bustle of everyday life. Furthermore, the presence of devotees and people shows that this church is not merely a detached historical relic, but a living sacred space deeply woven into the daily lives of the people of Santa Rosa.
artworks.our_judgement: The Santa Rosa de Lima Parish Church is a remarkable example of religious and cultural architecture. By maintaining its historic integrity and maintaining a strong spiritual presence in daily life, it succeeds both aesthetically and structurally. Its long-standing craftsmanship, proportion, and active involvement in the local community attest to its high artistic and cultural value.

artworks.location: Parokya ni Santa Rosa de Lima (Santa Rosa, Laguna)
artworks.written_by: Francisco, Athaliah L. & Molato, Eliyah G.
artworks.what_we_see: This painting depicts a young woman identified as Saint Rose of Lima. She is shown wearing a nun’s headdress, made up of a white wimple and a black veil, topped with a crown of red roses. Her eyes are light in color, and her expression appears calm and gentle. In the background are two architectural details of the parish church, with the exterior of the church on the left against a blue backdrop, and the altar inside the church on the right against a pink backdrop. At the bottom of the canvas, her name is written along with her birth and death dates.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artist positioned the woman at the center of the composition and facing forward. The contrast between the black veil and the white wimple draws the viewer’s attention directly to her face. The red roses stand out sharply against the dark veil and the pale backdrop behind her. The background is divided into two contrasting tones, blue and white on the left and pink and gold on the right, which helps balance the painting. This use of color and symmetry gives the painting a sense of order and stability, keeping the focus on the saint’s serene expression.
artworks.our_interpretation: Since St. Rose of Lima is Santa Rosa’s patroness, the portrait shows local devotion and identity, naming her after an architecture, making her feel like a local, not just a distant historical saint. The rose crown around her head isn’t just a decoration, it represents her name “Rose” also it speaks about the beauty and suffering she has been through. According to the story, the spike under her crown signifies that she hides her suffering and devotion to others.
artworks.our_judgement: It is a successful piece of devotional/community art that is both technically sound and emotionally approachable, despite having a reverential rather than experimental goal. Its strength is derived less from universal artistic innovation and more from local meaning.

artworks.what_we_see: The painting centers on a black and white figure of a boy smiling with a red clown nose, wearing a Barong Tagalog, and drinking from a cup while sitting on a small stool. On his head sits a bright and smiling hamburger. Two skin-toned hands extend from the bottom corners, pointing directly at him. He is surrounded by shallow water filled with colorful items like a white paper boat, red apples, a yellow rubber duck, a compass, and a cardboard box. The blue sky above him features a Rubik’s cube, a winged melting clock, a snow globe, and flying birds.
artworks.personal_analysis: The boy serves as the main focal point, created through a sharp contrast between his monochromatic grayscale body and the vibrant and highly saturated colors of the surrounding environment. The composition relies on formal balance, placing the boy in the center while two large hands at the bottom form diagonal implied lines that point directly toward him. Smooth shading and value create realistic implied textures on his Barong Tagalog and the surrounding objects. The artist plays with exaggerated scale by making the hands and hamburger hat unusually large, while strategically distributing colorful floating objects across the canvas to establish rhythm and visual movement before drawing the viewer’s attention back to the central subject.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork reflects on life's decisions, showing how every choice and ambition carries a corresponding consequence and responsibility. The painting creates a bittersweet mood, capturing a child holding onto joy and imagination while stepping up to face the realities of life. Although dressed in a formal Barong Tagalog that represents societal expectations, the grayscale boy wears a red clown nose and a smiling hamburger hat as a playful coping mechanism to face these burdens with courage. The two oversized hands pointing at him emphasize the constant societal judgement and accountability tied to one's actions. Floating symbols like the melting clock, submerged compass, and Rubik's cube signify lost time, uncertain paths, and the complex choices of growing up.
artworks.our_judgement: The painting is good because it skillfully blends to deliver a powerful message about responsibility and choice. Its composition and smooth execution make it both visually engaging and emotionally impactful, effective in provoking deep thought from the viewer.

artworks.what_we_see: This painting shows a woman standing in the center against a plain black background. She wears a golden-yellow Filipiniana blouse, a pearl necklace and earrings, and a small tiara placed across the ocean scenery on her headpiece. On her head rests an elaborate crab headpiece with a blue face and an ocean scene with fishermen painted across its shell, with large crab claws decorated with vibrant folk-art patterns on both sides. In front of her, she holds a brown woven basket filled with silver-gray fish. In the top right corner, a small red full moon floats in the dark background.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artist uses central symmetry and sharp contrast to highlight the main subject. The bright golden-yellow dress and blue headpiece stand out against the solid black background, drawing immediate attention to the figure. Smooth textures on her skin contrast with the detailed patterns on the crab claws and the woven basket. Balanced warm and cool colors guide the viewer’s eyes naturally from her face up to the intricate ocean scene and tiara on her crab headpiece.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork honors the dignity, hard work, and cultural heritage of everyday Filipino workers. By dressing the woman in a traditional Filipiniana blouse, pearls, and a tiara, the painting treats a humble street vendor like royalty. The elaborate crab headpiece containing an ocean scene with fishermen symbolizes how her community’s coastal livelihood is deeply tied to her identity. Set against a dark background with a red moon, her calm expression and vibrant folk-art patterns create a proud and respectful tone that celebrates local tradition and honest labor.
artworks.our_judgement: The artist successfully creates a powerful piece by elevating a simple fish vendor into a regal, through details and clean composition. The creative use of the crab headpiece as a canvas for coastal life makes the artwork both visually captivating and culturally resonant.

artworks.what_we_see: The painting features a young man wearing a traditional woven hat called sakalot, a short-sleeved dress shirt, dark blue shorts and black shoes where one of which is drenched in water. He is standing on shallow water with his right hand holding a pole and the other is freely extended outwards, his palms facing forward. Positioned directly between his legs and resting on the sand at the water's edge is a large turtle with a dark brown dome-shaped shell, a textured yellowish-brown head, and thick, scaly dark legs with black claws, its head turned toward the right. Silver fishes are scattered around the area; some are still in the shallow sea while some are laying on the sand. Behind the two central figures, there are a group of people that are crossing the water carrying lanterns and a long wooden pole. In the distant background, a white colonial-style stone church stands with a tiered bell tower and the sky above it shows a sunset with an orange sun low over the horizon and blue-toned clouds streaking across a dark blue sky.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artist mainly uses light and color to organize the composition. He used the warm and golden light from the sunset to highlight the central subject of the painting, the man and the turtle while the group of people in the water are shadowed with darker tones of blue. The usage of this color temperature acts as a divider between the two different areas. With the topic of dividers at hand, the man's hand acts as a diagonal visual barrier. Furthermore, the aforementioned division is supported by the shape wherein the man and the turtle in the foreground are rendered as solid, well-defined forms, whereas the crowd in the background is depicted as smaller, indistinct silhouettes. The naturalistic handling of texture is evident in the detailed rendering of the turtle's ridged carapace, the woven texture of the salakot, and the reflective quality of the wet sand. The vertical church tower on the right offsets the horizontal shoreline and the boy's pose, keeping the composition stable. The boy's raised hand and gaze remain the focal point due to his bright lighting and central placement.
artworks.our_interpretation: The painting tells a story of defiance. The man is wearing an outfit similar to the people behind him, which suggests they are his own community. His outstretched hand shows he is standing between the turtle and his people not only physically but also morally to protect the animal from harm. The church behind the crowd indicates they may be connected to religion, their actions influenced by a specific order or belief. The warm, golden light on the man and the turtle contrasts with the cooler, shadowed crowd, reinforcing the idea that he represents hope, compassion and a more enlightened relationship with nature, while the group behind him represents older customs and collective will.
artworks.our_judgement: The painting is highly memorable, the depiction of the relationship between man and animal is easily recognisable. The stance of the man was enough to provide contexts of why there was a crowd surging up from the sea. However, the title of the piece in itself felt quite disconnected to the artwork, as though there is still some context missing that wasn't provided enough by the elements in the painting.

artworks.what_we_see: This artwork is a three-panel painting showing three ballerinas dancing and placed in their own separate frames. The dancer on the left wears a red top paired with a flowing peach colored skirt, with her hair styled in a bun and one arm raised gracefully above her head. The dancer in the center wears a black top paired with a large flowing red skirt that is caught mid spinning. The dancer on the right wears a peach colored top and skirt with her body leaning and one arm stretched outward. Each dancer shows a different movement but together they create a sense of harmony and rhythm.
artworks.personal_analysis: The artist used a soft, muted green background across all three panels which allows the ballerinas and their flowing skirts to stand out as the main focus. The bright red skirt in the center panel creates a strong contrast against the peach tones of the two outer ballerinas, drawing the viewer’s eye toward the middle of the composition. Each dancer is captured in a different pose and movement, yet the following lines of their dresses and arms connect the three panels together visually. This use of varied poses combined with consistent color of background and floor creates a sense of rhythm and harmony across the piece despite each panel being separate.
artworks.our_interpretation: This artwork conveys a sense of grace, movement, and unity among the three dancers. The flowing dresses and different poses suggest freedom and individuality for each dancer. The shift of color in the center dancer’s skirt may represent a moment of passion or energy, suggesting that the center dancer could be the lead, while the two dancers in peach may represent supporting or background dancers. Displaying the three dancers together, each moving differently yet in harmony may symbolize connection with each other.
artworks.our_judgement: This artwork is successful in showing elegance and movement through its use of color and flowing shapes. The bold red skirt in the center draws attention to that dancer without taking too much from the other two. The different poses across the three panels give the piece a sense of both individuality and harmony among the dancers. The three-panel format helps express togetherness and shared rhythm. Altogether, the artwork creates a graceful and expressive portrayal of dance and connection.

artworks.what_we_see: The painting depicts a lively, nostalgic street scene along Calle Crisologo in Vigan under a glowing sun and historic colonial architecture. The cobblestone street and balconies are filled with locals, vendors, and children wearing traditional Filipino clothing. In the foreground and along the street, vendors carry colorful balloons, baskets, and taho buckets, while a boy plays guitar to serenade a girl amidst families and couples. A horse-drawn carriage sits further down the central street, all painted in a warm, vivid color palette of yellows, reds, blues, and oranges.
artworks.personal_analysis: The warm palette of bright yellows, oranges, and reds illuminates the scene with a joyful, festive glow. The artist contrasts structured geometric buildings with soft, rounded characters, featuring her signature round-eyed people that give her figures a range of emotions. Repeated patterns across the windows, balconies, and crowded streets create visual rhythm and lively movement throughout the composition.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork expresses a deep sense of nostalgia and love for traditional Filipino culture and community life. Through everyday scenes like street vendors and romantic serenades, the painting highlights the simple joys and warmth of togetherness under the historic colonial architecture of Calle Crisologo.
artworks.our_judgement: This is successful artwork because it skillfully blends techniques with a warm, lively composition that captures the charm and warmth of Filipino heritage.

artworks.what_we_see: A colorful scene of villagers gathered around a small campfire at night. While others sing, dance, and shake tambourines and maracas, two men in the center play guitars. A man roasts a fish on the right, while a woman on the left holds a tray of bread. A large moon hangs over the trees in a starry sky, a nipa hut stands in the background, and a pineapple and other fruits sit in the corner.
artworks.personal_analysis: The community's long, stretched faces, large, heavy-lidded eyes, and straightforward shapes, almost like cutouts, give the painting a playful, storybook vibe. Rich and striking hues are used, with warm oranges, yellows, and greens for the people and plants and deep blue and purple for the night sky. Your eyes are constantly scanning the scene because the crowd is positioned in a loose circle around the fire, which is in the center. The vibe is further enhanced by the vibrant and busy patterns on their clothing.
artworks.our_interpretation: The artwork seems to be a celebration of Filipino community life. The bayanihan spirit, where people gather to cook, eat, and spend time together, is symbolized by the nipa hut, food, music, and shared fire. Although everyone is participating in a different activity, they are all a part of the same group, demonstrating that happiness is a shared experience rather than something you do alone.
artworks.our_judgement: It's a warm, cheerful painting with an immediately recognizable strong style. It's easy to relate to because it brings back memories of actual get-togethers and fiestas and serves as a helpful reminder that ordinary, everyday moments spent with family and neighbors are worthy of celebration.

about.group_introduction: We are a group of students documenting the art hiding in plain sight around Santa Rosa, Laguna — from museum-grade works to pieces made by our own neighbors.
about.why_we_created_statement: We built this exhibit because so much local art goes unlabeled and unexplained. We wanted a place where a painting on a barangay hall wall gets the same care and context as something hanging in a museum.
